subject: Private GPU pool: throttle curves, latency budgets & headroom matrices
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, ops@edgeworks.io
Date: 2027-05-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private GPU pool: throttle curves, latency budgets & headroom matrices

Team / EdgeWorks,

Attaching a first-pass of the capacity/runbook artifacts we discussed for the on‑prem private GPU pool. Goal: set concrete throughput targets, define util headroom, and agree scale/fallback triggers so that ACME/EdgeWorks deployments meet our p95 latency and availability SLOs while keeping cost predictable.

High-level targets I baked in:
- Steady-state target: 800 concurrent inference streams for 8k-token average workloads (~2.2k tokens/sec aggregate per node profile).
- P95 latency budget: 120ms for short-generation routes (<=128 tokens), 450ms for heavy routes (>=1k tokens) across the private cluster; tail mitigation via KV cache warmup and request prefix routing.
- Target utilization thresholds: soft scale at 60% GPU utilization, hard scale/add-node at 75%. Emergency throttle/fallback to hosted model at 90%.

Primary asks:
1) Dev: validate the throughput per-GPU numbers and whether our kernel mix assumptions (bf16 quant + Triton fused kernels) change the util thresholds.
2) Naomi: network egress/ingress requirements and hot‑path affinity (what cross‑rack limits force different headroom?).
3) Laura: procurement/contract constraints for reserved capacity and maintenance windows (EdgeWorks needs a CZ window).
4) EdgeWorks: feasibility of warm standby nodes and burst networks; any hard limits we must know about (rack power, NIC oversubscription).

Attachments: throttle-curve-matrix-20270509.xlsx (matrix of WH/scale triggers + simulation rows), onprem-nettopology-v1.drawio (proposed rack/network layout).

Next step: 30-min sync if there are disagreements. I can host Thursday 11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throttle curves, latency budgets & headroom matrices

On 2027-05-09T10:12:00-07:00, Vivek Kulkarni wrote:
> High-level targets I baked in:
> - Steady-state target: 800 concurrent inference streams for 8k-token average workloads (~2.2k tokens/sec aggregate per node profile).
> - P95 latency budget: 120ms for short-generation routes (<=128 tokens), 450ms for heavy routes (>=1k tokens)

Quick pass from runtime side: the aggregate numbers look directionally reasonable but a few clarifications and caveats:

1) Baseline per-GPU profile: the 2.2k tokens/sec assumes A100-40GB with our current bf16 kernels and a KV cache hit rate of ~65%. If KV warmup is lower (<=30%) for cold starts, effective tokens/sec drops by ~30%.
2) Kernel mix matters: long-context attention windows push memory pressure and reduce effective batch parallelism. For sustained >=4k-token avg requests we should expect 18–25% lower throughput.
3) Util thresholds: soft scale at 60% is good for avoiding tail latencies, but for Dense-serving (no quantization) I'd nudge hard-add at 72% not 75% — the delta buys headroom for transient spikes.
4) Autoscaler behavior: prefer a cooldown of 90s for scale-ups and 5m for scale-downs; short cooldowns cause oscillation with bursty traffic.

I added an extra simulation tab in the workbook with two annotated scenarios (cold start daily batch at 03:00 UTC; lunchtime traffic surge). See comments on rows B14–B27.

Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: throttle-curve-matrix-20270509.xlsx (updated - dev comments)]

From: ops@edgeworks.io <ops@edgeworks.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throttle curves, latency budgets & headroom matrices

Vivek / team,

Thanks for the doc — helpful. A few site constraints from EdgeWorks side that will change the headroom calculus:

- Rack power: dense racks are limited to 18kW on the floor we plan to use, which limits us to 4x A100-80GB per rack (when combined with NVMe and switches). That means cross‑rack traffic for >4 node deployments will be significant.
- NIC oversubscription: top-of-rack (ToR) is 2:1 oversubscribed at peak; for steady high-qps low-latency traffic we recommend colocating inference and request routing in the same rack when possible.
- Warm standby: feasible, but the cluster-level licensing requires standby nodes be reported for licensing (cost impact). Warm standby with drained ranks is ok; cold-boot time is ~6–8 minutes for full model checkpoint load on A100 depending on networked storage throughput.

Action items from our side: we can guarantee 40Gbps per host baseline and will prioritize 100Gbps for the 2 critical racks if you sign the network uplift addendum (we attached the addendum in the vendor portal). Also, if you want <200ms p95 for heavy routes cross‑rack we recommend a 30% per-rack headroom (so your scale thresholds should be more conservative).

— EdgeWorks Ops
ops@edgeworks.io
[Attachment: edgeworks-network-addendum-20270510.pdf (pdf stub)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, ops@edgeworks.io
Date: 2027-05-10T11:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throttle curves, latency budgets & headroom matrices

Adding a couple of concrete networking constraints and monitoring asks: 

- Egress/Ingress: plan for 10Gbps additional headroom per rack for KV-sync traffic during cache warmups. If you expect frequent cache churn (multiple model versions), bump to 25Gbps.
- TCP tuning: enable BBR v2 and increase the default rmem/wmem for hosts doing model checkpoint transfers; I've pasted a sample sysctl set in the drive link.
- Observability: must emit per-host GPU utilization, per-pod queue depth, and per-request path latency with tags for rack-id and model-version. We need these metrics wired to the Console before first cutover.

On the scale plan: agree with Dev to use 60% soft and 72% hard. For cross-rack deployments, treat 55% as soft and 68% as hard (EdgeWorks rack oversubscription + power constraints).

Naomi
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-11T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throttle curves, latency budgets & headroom matrices

Thanks everyone — summary and immediate decisions below: 

Decisions (agreed):
- Utilization thresholds: soft scale at 60% (in-rack), hard add-node at 72% (in-rack). Cross-rack: soft 55% / hard 68%.
- Headroom reserve: 30% per-rack for heavy routes to preserve p95s; warm-standby permitted but counted in licensing (EdgeWorks).
- Cold-start mitigation: implement prefix-based cache warmup plus prefetch job that runs at T-5m for scheduled bursts; expect 6–8m cold boot for full checkpoint loads.
- Autoscaler tuning: scale-up cooldown 90s, scale-down cooldown 5m; add a rate-limiter for scale-downs to avoid oscillation.
- Observability: Naomi will own wiring metrics to Console (per-host GPU util, queue depth, path latency) before cutover.

Open items / next steps:
- Laura: confirm contract window & sign network uplift addendum from EdgeWorks (link in thread).
- Dev: update spreadsheet to variant the long-context kernel assumptions and mark a contingency column for 20% perf delta.
- EdgeWorks: confirm NIC uplift timeline and provide final power/per-rack layout by EOD Friday.
- Schedule a 30-min rollout dry run next Wednesday 11:00 PT to exercise warm standby and KV warmup.

If no objections by EOD Friday I'll lock these values into the runbook and ops playbooks.

Vivek
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
